expect.note: every evals/report/<ts>-<suite>.json cited in docs/, specs/, tasks/, README.md, src/, evals/golden|adversarial/, .github/, or prompts/ must exist on disk, EXCEPT two literal filenames -- 29991231-235959-fast.json (a repro instruction in tasks/reviews/pr20-r1.json tells a reviewer to CREATE that file, not evidence of a real run) and 20260827-200410-fast.json (PR #66 R5 in tasks/reviews/pr66-r1.json is a finding ABOUT that aborted no-venv report, and its resolution line records that it was DELETED -- the name is the record of a removal, not a claim of evidence) -- every other citation under tasks/reviews/, including the 8 real ones in review resolution files, is guarded like any other -- and EXCEPT files under src/browser/fixtures/, which are captured pages, not prose this repo wrote: the M41 inspector snapshot renders the other project's capability table and names a benchmark report in ITS evals/report/. That exclusion is a directory prefix, the shape PR #20 R20 caught blinding this guard, so `exclude_exactly` pins its width the way `skip_exactly` pins the literal filename -- widening a scan removes findings silently, so a pin is the only thing that can notice.; and no routine report file sits in evals/report/ uncited by anything in scope — the reverse direction, with ADR-012's policy-exempt kinds named explicitly; and a pass-rate figure sitting next to a citation must be the one that report actually holds — resolving is not supporting

provenance: ADR-012 pruned 124 uncited routine gate dumps out of evals/report/ (159 files, 4.8MB -> 34 files), keeping on disk only the ones cited as evidence elsewhere in the repo. Nothing enforced that those citations stay resolvable once that prune candidates were deleted, or once a future edit renames/deletes a currently-cited report -- the exact failure mode this repo already guards against for case ids (support-matrix-cites-real-cases) but never had for report files. Watched red by temporarily renaming a cited report on disk (evals/report/20260816-002725-fast.json, cited from specs/decisions/ADR-002-performance-thresholds.md) -> missing_reports: ['20260816-002725-fast.json']; renamed back -> green. PR #20 R20: the exclusion was a `tasks/reviews` PATH PREFIX, wide enough to blind this guard to 8 genuine review citations (not just the one synthetic literal) -- verified by moving evals/report/20260821-121835-fast.json aside: passed=True even though it is real evidence, because its only citations lived under the excluded path. Narrowed to the one literal filename; the same repro now correctly fails (missing_reports: ['20260821-121835-fast.json']), moved back -> green. `skip_exactly` pins the exclusion set itself so a future edit cannot silently widen it back into a path prefix without this case going red. T-R19 (P1) closed here 2026-08-28. This case was ONE-DIRECTIONAL: it resolved citation -> file and never enumerated `evals/report/*.json` to ask whether each file is cited by anything. That is how the merge at `94f1a42`/`7a2869a` re-added 41-46 uncited routine gate dumps ADR-012 had just pruned; 38 of them (20 `fast`, 18 `invariant`) were deleted BY HAND, which is a cleanup, not a guard. The exempt kinds are ADR-012's own ruling ("non-prunable by policy regardless of citation") and are declared in `expect` rather than hard-coded, so widening them is a visible edit to a case file: a `live`/`soak`/`ablation`/`bench` report is a measurement nothing can reproduce, while a routine `fast`/`invariant` dump is reproducible by running the suite, which is exactly why citation is what earns it a place on disk. T-M32-10 (P1) closed here 2026-08-28. A citation that RESOLVES is not a citation that SUPPORTS: ADR-020 claimed "`live` suite 9/9 after this change" beside a report whose score is 0.889 — 8/9, `live-ol-edition-title` failing — and nothing could see it, so a green claim hung on a red artifact inside a review's own surface. The nearest `N/M` figure of the report's own size, within 400 characters of the citation, must equal what the report holds. NEAREST, and that took two tries: the first rule was "some figure in the window matches", and replaying ADR-020's own defect passed it — because the paragraph now explains its history and carries BOTH 8/9 and 9/9, so the wrong one satisfied the check. A paragraph legitimately shows its work; the figure a citation is offered as evidence for is the one beside it. Two exemptions, both measured rather than assumed. Soak reports have `results` whose entries carry no `passed` key, so counting them read every soak row as a failure and turned a correct "10/10" into a false positive. And `tasks/reviews/` is exempt from the CLAIM check while staying inside the citation check: `pr34-r4.json` is finding R17 REPORTING this exact defect, so a reviewer quoting a false pair is the record of the finding rather than a new instance, and editing that text to satisfy a regex would delete the evidence — the same ruling `REPORT_CITATION_SKIP` already makes one field over. Watched red by re-pointing ADR-020's sentence at the report it originally cited: `{nearest_claim: "9/9", report_is: "8/9"}`.

triage.note: same shape as support-matrix-cites-real-cases and adr-header-and-index: this guards a bookkeeping contract (does the evidence a document points at still exist), not the product, so it stays pure code with no network and no browser. It does not grade whether a citation is still an honest measurement of the claim next to it -- that is a human judgment act, same boundary the matrix case draws.
